newsitem.title: CANADA: TD Bank sees Canada gov'ts meeting targets.
newsitem.headline: TD Bank sees Canada gov'ts meeting targets.

text.p: Canada's federal and provincial governments will likely meet or better their fiscal targets this year, Toronto-Dominion Bank economists said in a report released on Monday.
The annual report on government finances noted both Canada's federal and provincial governments have made great progress towards balancing budgets in recent years.
"Seven provincial governments -- all with the exception of Ontario, Quebec and Newfoundland -- plan to balance their budgets this year," TD senior economist Teresa Chandler said in a statement.
The report noted that Canada's provincial governments committed to lowering their combined deficit from 1.3 percent of GDP this year to almost zero three years from now.

TD economists have ranked the provinces on their progress in achieving a stable balanced-budget position. Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island were given the top ranking.

Over the past year, financial markets have regained confidence in the ability of Canadian governments to achieve fiscal targets, Chandler said. This has sharply narrowed risk premia incorporated in Canadian interest rates.
